summary: Interleaved fallback fanout causing elevated 5xx rate and streaming disconnects
description:
Issue summary:
Customer Acme Retail is observing a sharp rise in 5xx responses and streaming disconnects for a subset of streaming and long-prompt requests since 2026-03-13 10:22 UTC. Errors correlate with tenant-specific fallback routing activity where the primary model variant was temporarily unavailable and requests were routed to fallback variants.

Impact:
- Elevated 5xx rate (502/503/504) for ~12% of requests from the customer over a 45 minute window, causing degraded UX in production chat and occasional session resets.
- Affected workloads include streaming chat and bulk small-batch embedding requests.
- Customer reported increased client-side retries and a spike in visible latency.

Environment:
- Dedicated tenant (Acme Retail) on prod us-east-1 using reserved capacity cluster: redwood-dedicated-ue1-22
- Traffic pattern: mix of streaming chat sessions and short embedding uploads with median seq length 320 tokens.

Observed behavior:
- api-gateway returned 502/503 and streaming connections dropped; many upstream runtime workers restarted during the window.
- Autoscaler triggered extra ephemeral runtimes during the storm, which aggravated prefetched KV eviction and increased model load churn.

Expected behavior:
- Fallback routing should limit concurrent fanout, respect cool-downs, and not cascade into autoscaler-induced warmup storms that overload proxy/threadpools.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Send sustained mixed streaming and small-batch embedding traffic to customer tenant redwood-tenant-acme with concurrency ~120 RPS and median prompt length ~300 tokens.
2) Simulate transient model load error on primary variant (inject 503 for 30s) to trigger fallback policy.
3) Observe upstream fanout: gateway routes to 3 fallback variants, runtime prefetch warms, autoscaler adds ephemeral workers, KV cache thrash starts and leads to runtime restarts and 502s.

comments: 2026-03-13T11:00:00Z - Maya Chen (Support): Initial triage: escalated to SRE; sent customer guidance to reduce client-side retry windows.

2026-03-13T11:10:27Z - Priya Patel (SRE): Observed fallback storm; disabling automatic fallback for tenant as short-term mitigation. Patch deployed to routing plane to ignore fallback for tenant acme until root cause addressed.
2026-03-13T11:35:42Z - Javier Morales (Acme Retail): Confirmed error rates dropped after workaround; still seeing intermittent single-request failures. Asked for postmortem and permanent fix ETA.
2026-03-14T09:12:05Z - Liam O'Connor (Eng): Reproduced locally with load harness; created PR to add per-tenant fallback cooldown and circuit breaker: see PR #4521. Planning hotfix rollforward today.
2026-03-14T12:04:59Z - Product (Nadia Khan): Requested metrics dashboard update to surface fallback amplification for all dedicated tenants; assigned to Observability team.
investigation_notes: Hypothesis 1: Fallback routing multiplies outbound model requests when primary variants fail, and our routing currently lacks a strict per-tenant concurrency cap -> fanout amplification.

Hypothesis 2: Autoscaler reacted to queue growth by spinning up ephemeral runtimes without sufficient prewarm hysteresis, increasing memory pressure and causing kvcache thrashing and runtime watchdog restarts.

Key metrics: 5xx rate (tenant acme) spiked from baseline 0.8% to 12% between 10:22-11:05 UTC; kvcache eviction rate correlated strongly with runtime OOM/restart counts; apigw threadpool saturated at 98%.
resolution: Short-term workaround applied 2026-03-13 11:12 UTC: disabled automatic multi-variant fallback for tenant acme and increased fallback_cooldown to 120s. Result: 5xx rate returned near baseline and customer confirmed improved UX.

Medium-term fix: Merge and roll out PR #4521 adding per-tenant fallback concurrency limit and an aggressive circuit breaker that enters 'degraded-single-variant' mode instead of full fanout during model warmup. Target rollout window 2026-03-14 18:00 UTC with canary route.

Long-term actions: Update autoscaler hysteresis to delay ephemeral runtime creation during fallback storms; add kvcache prefetch backpressure signals to routing plane; create runbook for tenant-level fallback incidents and add alerting (alert: FallbackAmplificationDetected).
Follow-ups: Observability to add a per-tenant FallbackAmplification metric and SLO guardrail; SRE to run postmortem and update postmortem page (link to be added here once completed).
